text:
erin: Heads up — noticed a ~12% dip in account healthscore for EU customers after last night's CRM sync. Suspect consent flags got nulled, which is suppressing onboarding nudges in the playbook. Anyone else seeing this?
joel: saw the alert in telemetry at ~03:40 UTC. Querying now, will post numbers. :eyes:
sam: quick check — maybe partner import mapping changed? last deploy included partner_v2 schema.
joel: quick sample results: ran `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts WHERE region='EU' AND consent_status IS NULL;` -> 4,120 affected (out of ~35k EU accounts).
mo hit: hmm — I deployed partner_v2 yesterday. We changed field names: `gdpr_consent` -> `consent_status` but partner sends `consent_source` too; our mapping missed fallback, so some rows defaulted to null.
cs-bot: [automated] Playbook: "onboard_nudge_v2" suppressed for 4,120 accounts (triggered at 2025-11-05T03:42:10Z).
erin: OK, we need a safe remediation plan: dry-run backfill, privacy signoff, then real backfill + replay playbook triggers for those accounts. No mass emails until privacy confirms.
sam: proposed dry-run command (no writes):
```
./scripts/backfill_consents --source partner_v2 --dry-run --limit 5000
```
This will print candidate updates and a sample payload for the playbook re-enqueue.
joel: ran the dry-run (sample attached): 4,120 rows -> candidate consent_status = 'granted' if partner_consent = 'yes', else 'revoked' or 'unknown'.
mo hit: policy check — we cannot set consent to 'granted' without partner proof. Can set `consent_status='unknown'` and `consent_source='partner:v2'` so playbooks treat them as manual review. That avoids accidental opt-ins.
erin: good plan. Steps: 1) joel run dry-run and paste sample payload to thread (done). 2) privacy review (cc @privacy). 3) if approved, run backfill with `--commit` at low traffic window (11:30 UTC). 4) enqueue a replay job that only re-runs playbook logic for those account ids.
joel: volunteered to run dry-run now and to schedule commit run at 11:30 UTC if privacy ok.
privacy: can you include a small sample of partner-provided consent evidence (timestamp or consent_id) in the payload? we need that to validate setting anything other than 'unknown'.
joel: will include sample_id & timestamp in the next output. Example update SQL for commit (for ops runbook):
```
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET consent_status = COALESCE(partner_consent_map, 'unknown'), consent_source = 'partner:v2' WHERE region='EU' AND consent_status IS NULL AND partner_received_at IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5000;
COMMIT;
```
We'll run in batches.
erin: add this to the incident log and create a tiny runbook note. No outbound emails. If privacy clears, :thumbsup: to run at 11:30 UTC.
mo hit: small automation tweak — will add a validation step in the import mapping so future rows default to 'unknown' instead of null. I'll open a PR after the run.
sam: and add a metric alert for sudden null spikes on consent_status so we catch this earlier.
erin: assigning @joel to execute the planned run. I'll open a Confluence note and ping legal if privacy needs extra docs. Thanks all. :shipit:
joel: starting the dry-run now, will post results in ~10m.
joel: dry-run done — attaching csv sample (first 20 rows) and counts. Posting sample payload snippet below.
joel: sample payload: `{\"account_id\": 12345, \"partner_consent\": \"yes\", \"partner_received_at\": \"2025-11-04T22:01:02Z\"}`
erin: perfect. Privacy — can you review that sample?
privacy: reviewed sample, proof present for ~65% of affected rows. We approve setting `consent_status='granted'` only when partner_received_at is present and partner_consent='yes'. For the rest, set 'unknown' and mark for manual review.
erin: excellent. Joel — proceed with commit run at 11:30 UTC and then enqueue replay job for playbook. Keep this thread updated.
joel: will do. closing loop here after run. :white_check_mark:
